chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:
I asked him about a captive whom the polytheists capture, and prayer time approaches, but the one who captured him prevents him from praying. He said: 'He gestures with a nod.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: With a nod or gesture (a specific mode of abbreviated prayer)
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: The polytheists (specifically in the context of early Islamic conflicts)

ai.seo_question: How should a prisoner perform prayer if they are prevented from doing it fully by their captors?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the specific mode of prayer (salat al-taqdir) for a captive whose mobility is restricted by their captors, establishing that simple gesturing (i'nam) suffices when full physical postures are impossible. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of easing religious obligations according to the degree of constraint, distinguishing this scenario from the battlefield prayer (salat al-khawf) by focusing on static imprisonment rather than active combat. The ruling underscores the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating physical limitations while maintaining the essence of worship.
